claim: A risk-based definition of an investable theme is a basket with statistically significant transient residual-return correlation; significant baskets in the study also exhibited statistically significant trending.
impact_on_spec: Define themes from rolling residual co-movement and significance rather than fixed GICS labels; treat trend as a separately tested return signal.
limitations: The paper studies baskets supplied by an investment bank; it does not establish local strategy alpha or an optimal clustering horizon.

claim: Year-by-year text similarity from 10-K product descriptions can produce firm-specific, time-varying competitor networks that differ from fixed industries.
impact_on_spec: Use acceptance-time SEC business descriptions as one slow-moving graph layer for product-chain and competitor membership.
limitations: Product similarity is a network-construction method, not evidence that a long-only theme portfolio earns excess returns after costs.

claim: The cited study finds return predictability across economically linked customer and supplier firms, consistent with delayed incorporation of related-firm news under attention constraints.
impact_on_spec: Test whether price or narrative shocks propagate from theme leaders to verified customers and suppliers over 3-20 sessions.
limitations: The original long-short result predates the current market and does not prove persistence in a liquid long-only US implementation.

claim: Industry components explain a substantial portion of individual-stock momentum, and past-winning-industry portfolios were profitable in the study after several controls.
impact_on_spec: Retain group-level momentum as a deterministic baseline while replacing static industries with point-in-time dynamic clusters.
limitations: The evidence uses historical industries and does not establish that modern narrative clusters outperform after turnover and crowding costs.

claim: Google search-volume attention predicted higher prices over approximately the next two weeks in the study, followed by longer-run reversal.
impact_on_spec: Test short 3-10 and 10-20 session attention windows and preregister an overheat/reversal exit rather than extrapolating attention indefinitely.
limitations: The 2004-2008 Google-search sample may not transfer to modern news and social attention; search data licensing and PIT access remain separate constraints.

claim: News-text narrative factors in the cited study achieved higher out-of-sample Sharpe ratios and smaller pricing errors than standard characteristic-based factor models in that setting.
impact_on_spec: Evaluate structured PIT narrative acceleration as a separate modality with quant-only, combined, missing-modality and placebo controls.
limitations: The paper's Wall Street Journal corpus and factor-pricing design do not validate Open Composer data, prompts, clusters or trading returns.

claim: The cited NBER study reports that specialized ETFs lost about 30% in risk-adjusted terms over their first five years, consistent with launches catering to attention around overvalued themes.
impact_on_spec: Do not equate a fashionable thematic ETF with alpha; include crowding, late-entry, equal-weight and ex-post-best-symbol controls.
limitations: The result concerns specialized ETF launches, not every dynamically identified stock cluster or short-horizon trade.

claim: Comparative asset-pricing evidence attributes gains from trees and neural networks to nonlinear predictor interactions, with momentum, liquidity and volatility among dominant signals.
impact_on_spec: Use a bounded fold-local nonlinear ranker only after a matched deterministic feature baseline; keep liquidity and volatility interactions explicit.
limitations: Broad-equity academic results do not guarantee lift in a smaller dynamic-theme universe and may require more data than is locally available.

claim: The updated preprint reports that LLM headline scores predict post-headline drift, especially for small stocks and negative news, while strategy returns decline as LLM adoption rises.
impact_on_spec: Treat LLM news interpretation as a bounded candidate role and require local PIT packets, marginal lift, decay monitoring and deterministic fallback.
limitations: This is a preprint, not local alpha evidence; the first reaction is not necessarily tradable and reported returns may decay with adoption.

claim: Stanford's 2026 AI Index reports that global corporate AI investment more than doubled in 2025, private investment grew 127.5%, generative-AI investment grew more than 200%, and surveyed organizational AI adoption reached 88%.
impact_on_spec: Use AI as a current seed topic whose subchains must still pass price, breadth, liquidity and crowding gates; do not hard-code it as a permanent winner.
limitations: Investment and adoption statistics establish economic activity, not security-level excess return or timing.

claim: Stanford's 2026 AI Index reports global AI compute capacity growth of 3.3 times per year since 2022 to 17.1 million H100-equivalents and AI data-center power capacity of 29.6 GW in 2025.
impact_on_spec: Seed candidate links spanning semiconductors, memory, networking, cooling, data centers, power equipment and generation, then let the dynamic graph and return factors select current leaders.
limitations: Capacity statistics do not identify listed winners and can coexist with valuation compression or crowded positioning.

claim: IFR reports 542,000 industrial robots installed in 2024, 4.664 million units in operational use, and a forecast of 575,000 installations in 2025.
impact_on_spec: Use robotics as a seed graph covering components, motion control, sensing, machine vision, integrators and end applications, not as one fixed sector ETF.
limitations: Global unit demand does not imply near-term US-listed equity alpha and includes regions and private firms outside the tradable universe.

claim: IFR reports nearly 200,000 professional service robots sold in 2024, up 9%, including 102,900 transportation and logistics units, up 14%.
impact_on_spec: Allow the robotics graph to discover logistics and service-automation subthemes independently of industrial-robot classifications.
limitations: Sales statistics are aggregate and do not establish issuer-level revenue exposure, margins or stock timing.

claim: SEC submissions and XBRL APIs update throughout the day as filings are disseminated; the submissions API has a typical processing delay under one second.
impact_on_spec: Use EDGAR acceptance time as visible_at for immutable filing packets, with accession, fetched_at, content hash and prompt hash bound before factor use.
limitations: EDGAR access does not provide news coverage, transcript licensing or proof that a later historical fetch matches every decision-time rendering.

claim: Alpaca documents historical news coverage back to 2015 with an average of more than 130 articles per day, currently supplied by Benzinga.
impact_on_spec: Evaluate provider feasibility, but admit news into historical research only after first-seen, revision, timestamp and use-rights contracts pass; otherwise collect forward-only PIT packets.
limitations: The page does not by itself establish immutable first-seen timestamps, revision history, redistribution rights or paper-ready historical PIT replay.

claim: TQQQ targets three times the daily Nasdaq-100 return before fees and expenses; ProShares states that returns over periods longer than one day can differ significantly from the daily target because of path and volatility effects.
impact_on_spec: Benchmark against realized matched-window TQQQ CAGR, drawdown and capture ratios rather than assuming a constant three-times annual return.
limitations: Issuer objectives and risk disclosures do not predict future TQQQ returns or guarantee paper fills.

claim: Data-driven cross-stock lead-lag linkages in the cited study generated momentum not subsumed by factor or industry momentum, and the linkages varied faster over time because short-run comovement incorporated persistent links.
impact_on_spec: Build separate fast 3-5-session acceleration and 10-20-session propagation graph layers from decision-time residual returns; do not use a permanent sector or stock membership list.
limitations: The published result is not local Open Composer alpha evidence, does not identify a causal industry chain, and may not transfer to a liquid long-only high-beta portfolio after costs.
